column1: # Fire Emblem Engage (update 2.0.0 = v327680; Unity 2020.3.18f1, IL2CPP, SDK 12.3.7) on Android (keys in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Game profiles on Android")
# Its data is 206,899 files (15.6 GB, base + update + 2 DLC), 205,000 of them of at most 1 MB (5.3 GB): pushed one by one over adb (each file made on the device through
# Android's FUSE layer) the install ran at ~1 MB/s, 9-14 h, and a download from the data server would make one request per file. So the pack keeps those files in 64 MB
# tar bundles that the app unpacks itself (data_bundles), the rest on its own: 89 bundles (5.5 GB) and 1,496 files. Retroid Pocket Nova over the LAN, the first sync of
# an app that unpacked on one thread: 38 minutes (the list checked 3:45, the bundles 96 s, the large files 8:23, 103,656 small files unpacked 24 minutes); the unpack now
# runs on 8 threads in place (the files folder is f2fs with dirsync there, ~13 ms a file made): 42,031 files in 1:51.
# Retroid Pocket Nova (QCS8550, Adreno 740, Turnip T30), 2026-11-15, Korean: title, Continue, chapters 1 and 2, story scenes, the maps, battles and their battle scenes,
# played by the user and run with the battles delegated: 60 fps, 0 frames dropped on screen (p99 16.67 ms), GPU p50 4-5 ms; a first start's shader preparation 17 s.
# Its device lost at scene changes (three in 30 minutes: the GPU hung on the new linked pipelines of a scene) was Turnip's fast link reading the fragment stage's
# dynamic uniform buffers at the vertex stage's slots, fixed in the core (gfx_vk_shader.c vk_dyn_ubo_mode, c9da25e): with every pipeline linked at its draw
# (DM_VK_NOPREWARM=1) 2 of 2 runs lost the device at the first battle scene before, 0 of 3 after, a first start with empty caches among them; about 40 minutes since.
# Battle scenes' lawn went dark for about a second after a hit and came back at once (2026-11-16; the Switch: no change): for that second, while a hit's light is in the
# light table, the game draws the ground and grass with their point-lit variants, and the lit grass blades (fragment shader d31ff45e8a33bdf1) came out darker than the
# unlit ones (1912f94e9c44fab3) with the same bindings, constants, textures and pipeline state, their code the same but for the point-light loop, which added nothing
# there (no NaN either). Why is not found. Blades left out, or that shader replaced by the unlit one's code: no darkening (the knight's axe hit in chapter 2, recorded
# and measured each run). The profile's android_spv.d31ff45e8a33bdf1.spv is that replacement (shader_vk.py; source in the .glsl beside it): the blades no longer take
# a hit's light, the ground under them still does.
# From the profile upstream made on its own (2026-11-11, merged here 2026-11-16):
# The package keeps the name the experimental port used, so a port made with this profile installs over it and keeps its saves.
# On Qualcomm's own driver (512.676.53) an Engage Attack scene draws as white/black silhouettes (#122); a Turnip driver draws it right.
# Tested 2026-11-11 on the AYN Thor with Turnip 27.0.0-R2: the map, menus, battles and an Engage Attack with Marth; 60 fps (a few steps to 40), 0 dropped frames,
# footprint 1.1-1.4 GB, 0 audio underruns, no red log line.
# Left: textures sometimes feel late to appear (not measured)
